ref_text: The night was cold and very quiet. Most of the street was asleep, and the lamps hummed over the empty road. Somewhere far away, a train rolled past, and then the silence came back.

lines.text: You're his only alibi.
Tell them I was with you!
Your best friend's locked up for robbing a watch shop.
Last Tuesday, seven forty. Where were you?
The police have one blurry photo. He has you. What did you eat? Check your photos. Nobody photographs a Tuesday.
The stall. It was raining, you had ginger chai, you paid cash, twenty rupees. Remember?
The stall. It was raining. You had ginger chai. You paid cash, twenty rupees. Remember?
At the stall. It was raining, you had ginger chai, and you paid cash, twenty rupees. Remember?
The chaiwala remembers nothing. So what did you drink?
lines.text_kokoro: The [chaiwala](/ʧˈaɪwˌɑːlɑː/) remembers nothing. So what did you drink?

lines.text: How much did you pay?
That's what he told us.
One more. What did he drink?
He never said. You made that up.
Not one word about his evening, because he wasn't with you.
He was here.
The alibi holds. He can go.
Nothing happened, so you had no Tuesday. Now you've got the one he wrote.
He didn't need you to remember. He needed you not to.
Thanks, yaar. Next time, I'll pay.
Lie researchers call that an unanticipated question.
So ask your best friend one. Where were they last Tuesday at seven forty?
But first: what's on his wrist?
